newsitem.title: UK: IGC sees 1997 world coarse grains crop at record.
newsitem.headline: IGC sees 1997 world coarse grains crop at record.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday forecast 1997 world coarse grains production at a record 897 million tonnes.
This compares with an estimate for 1996 of 889 million.

"Better prospects for central and eastern Europe, Russia, Ukraine, the United States and some African countries may only be partly offset by reductions in output in the EU, Canada and Argentina," the IGC said.

The volume of trade will depend heavily on developments in far east Asia, which accounts for around half of global imports. Growth in compound feed output, especially for pig and poultry rations, should lead to a further expansion in demand for maize, in particular, the IGC said.
World trade in 1997-98 in all coarse grains was projected at 90 million tonnes, up from 88 million for 1996-97.
The IGC also forecast record consumption, at 895 million tonnes compared to 865 million in 1996-97. Most of the increase is expected to be in the U.S. and China.
On current assumptions, world stocks could rise by two million tonnes to 116 million tonnes at the end of 1997-98. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
